title: Josiah
lead: King of Judah about 640–609 BC, who came to the throne at eight. In his reign a scroll of the law, widely identified with Deuteronomy, was found in the temple, and he carried out the most sweeping religious reform in Judah's history. He died at Megiddo facing Pharaoh Neco.

sections.b: A man of God names Josiah three centuries ahead (1 Kings 13:2). His reign is told in 2 Kings 22–23 and 2 Chronicles 34–35. Jeremiah and Zephaniah were active in his day (Jeremiah 1:2; Zephaniah 1:1), and Jeremiah praises him as a king who did justice and defended the poor (Jeremiah 22:15–16). The mourning for him became a custom (2 Chronicles 35:24–25). Matthew 1:10–11 lists him among Jesus' ancestors.
